description: Treemap explorer that finds what is filling a disk, marks it, and removes it (Rust + GPUI, GUI-only binary).
##: Comment field (Scoop ignores it). Key order does not matter to Scoop's parser;
this file follows the ordering used by the official buckets: version, description,
homepage, license, comments/notes, architecture, bin, shortcuts, checkver, autoupdate.
Settings file: disktree is a portable single-file exe (no installer, no DLLs, static
CRT, GUI subsystem), but it keeps exactly one preference OUTSIDE the install dir:
One line of text holding the scan/CPU preset (miser | balanced | aggressive |
drain-my-battery). The upstream code deliberately never writes beside the exe, so
Scoop's persist cannot redirect it. It is created only when the user changes Power
Efficiency in the app (a plain run writes nothing), and scoop uninstall leaves it
behind; delete %APPDATA%\disktree to reset to the default. No registry keys, no
services, no admin rights required (elevation is optional, for the NTFS MFT scan).
notes: disktree is a portable single-file GUI app, but it keeps one small settings file OUTSIDE
the install directory (by design - the upstream code refuses to write next to the exe):
It holds one line of text (the scan/CPU preset, e.g. 'balanced'). It is created only the
first time you change Power Efficiency in the app; a plain run writes nothing. Scoop's
uninstall does not remove it - delete %APPDATA%\disktree to reset to the default.
No registry keys are written, and no admin rights are needed (elevation is optional and
only offered in-app for the NTFS MFT fast scan of a whole drive).
